situation.note: 11 years in dubai sending money home. brothers wedding, fathers heart surgery, both this year. my wife wants to go back to india. everyone needs something from me and I don't know what I need

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being the one who always provides to being the one who asks what he needs, with a mind that can finally settle.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the restlessness and the exhaustion, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the mind that cannot settle is not broken. It is a mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest.
week_beats.steady: You hold that a mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest is not a mind that is broken.
week_beats.act: You try giving your mind one quiet minute to rest, and letting one person know what you need before you decide anything else.
week_beats.story: A man who has been the provider for his family for years shows you what it looks like to ask what he needs.

understanding.core_struggle: An eleven-year migrant who has been sending money home faces his father's surgery and his brother's wedding, while his wife wants to return and he no longer knows what he needs.
understanding.mirror: You send money home for eleven years, and now the phone rings with two different needs at once.
understanding.insight: You have been the one who sends, the one who pays, the one who decides. The exhaustion is not in the work. It is in having no one left to ask what you need.

queries.hook: A mind that has been the provider for eleven years and now cannot settle, with no hour of its own and no answer to what it needs. My parents are getting older far away.
queries.diagnose: When the mind is never given one quiet minute to rest, it begins to run after results it cannot hold; restlessness grows from a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
queries.steady: The mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest is not a mind that is broken; it is a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
queries.act: Give your mind one quiet minute to rest, and let one person know what you need before you decide anything else.
queries.story: A man who has been the provider for his family for years, facing his own exhaustion and the question of what he needs, and finding the courage to ask.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.for_you: You are not the mind; thoughts come and go before the silent witness that watches them and is never disturbed.

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.for_you: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verse.line: A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.
verse.translation: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, the king who has laid down his kingdom. He is describing the inner life of the wise. He says the fool is restless even when doing nothing, while the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing. The point is that peace is not a place you arrive at or a state you force. It is a quality of attention. It is how you hold ordinary life, whether it is full or empty.
verse.for_you: You have been the one who sends, the one who pays, the one who decides. The exhaustion is not in the work. It is in having no one left to ask what you need. This verse says the calm of the wise is not in doing nothing.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you are doing something ordinary and your mind is not already three steps ahead.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own closing chapter, where the question is not what you do next, but how you hold what is already here.
asks: How do I stop being the one who decides everything?
What if I am not skilled enough to stay calm?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker: that's a settled mind.
verse.translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image used for the yogi of controlled mind practising union with the self.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to sit and focus. The setting is the middle of a great war. Arjuna is exhausted and confused. Krishna tells him to find a steady seat and to bring the wandering mind back again and again. The mind is compared to a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker. This means the mind stops moving and becomes still.
verse.for_you: Your mind has been moving between eleven years in Dubai and a father's surgery and a wife who wants to return. It is trying to hold all of it at once. This is not a broken mind.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in your room after a long day of work, and you bring your attention back to your own breath.
asks: How do I bring my mind back to one thing?
What does it mean to let my mind settle?

verse.speaker: Bhishma
verse.setting: Gautama orders his son Chirakari, 'the slow one', to kill his mother; the son deliberates, and saves them all.
verse.sanskrit: एवं सर्वेषु कार्येषु विमृश्य पुरुषस्ततः / चिरेण निश्चयं कृत्वा चिरं न परितप्यते
verse.line: Think it over and decide slowly, and you'll spend far less time in regret.
verse.translation: So, in every matter, a person should think it over and decide slowly; then he does not suffer regret for long.
verse.why: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

prasang.title: Chirakari, the one who acts slowly
prasang.summary: In a jealous rage, the sage Gautama orders his son Chirakari to kill his mother and storms off. Chirakari, famous for slowness, weighs a father's word against a mother's worth for so long that Gautama returns, regretful, and finds them both alive.
prasang.story_hook: Ordered by his furious father to kill his mother, Chirakari did what he always did: he thought about it.
prasang.lesson: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

verse.meaning: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that in every matter, a person should think it over and decide slowly, so that they do not suffer regret for long. The story behind this is of the sage Gautama, who in a jealous rage orders his son Chirakari to kill his mother. Chirakari is known as the slow one, and he weighs his father's command against the value of his mother's life so thoroughly that Gautama returns and cancels the order.
verse.for_you: Now your partner wants to return and your parents need more care. Thinking it over slowly does not mean you are abandoning them.
verse.try_today: Before you answer any message from home, take one minute to sit with the question.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your quiet room with a message waiting, and you could decide how to answer it.
asks: How do I slow down when everyone needs me now?
Can I ask for help without letting my family down?

verse.speaker: Bhishma
verse.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verse.sanskrit: वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रमनाथा च स्वसा गुरुः / कुलीनः पण्डित इति रक्ष्या निःस्वः स्वशक्तितः / गृहे वासयितव्यास्ते धन्यमायुष्यमेव च
verse.line: An aging relative, a friend in need, a sister with no support: make room for them as you can.
verse.translation: An aged relative, a friend, a sister with no one to support her, a teacher, a person of good family or learning who has fallen poor: protect them as you are able, and give them a place in your home.
verse.why: A good life is built from daily conduct: kind words, respect for elders, no mockery.

prasang.title: Bhishma on everyday conduct
prasang.summary: Asked what makes a life long and good, Bhishma answers: conduct. Be slow to anger and honest, greet your parents each morning, never mock anyone, and remember that a cruel word lodges in the heart.
prasang.lesson: A good life is built from daily conduct: kind words, respect for elders, no mockery.

verse.meaning: Bhishma is telling Yudhishthira how to live a long and good life. He says to be slow to anger and honest, to greet your parents each morning, and never to mock anyone. A cruel word lodges in the heart. He also says to protect an aging relative or a friend in need as you are able, and to give them a place in your home. A good life is built from these small acts of daily conduct.
verse.for_you: You have spent eleven years sending money home. Now your father has had surgery and your brother has married. You are the one who pays and decides. But a good life is built from these small acts of daily conduct.
verse.try_today: Give your mind one quiet minute of rest before you decide anything else today.
verse.scene_line: You are the one who pays and decides, and your mind is the aging relative with no support.
asks: How do I give my mind a place in my home?
What is one small act of daily conduct I can do today?
How do I protect my mind as I protect my parents?

story.title: Kausalya lets Ram go
story.story_hook: His mother had waited seventeen years for this day, and it was taken from her in a morning.
story.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.
story.lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.

anchor.speaker: Ram
anchor.setting: Ram's mother wants to follow him into exile; he asks her instead to stay and look after his grieving father.
anchor.sanskrit: यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः॥ श्रमं नावाप्नुयात् किंचिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु। दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्॥ राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।
anchor.line: When I'm gone, look after him. Don't let his grief wear him down.
anchor.translation: Take care that when I am gone the king does not wear himself out with grief for his son, that this terrible sorrow does not destroy him. Look after the old king's welfare always.
anchor.why: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.

prasang.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.
prasang.story_hook: His mother had waited seventeen years for this day, and it was taken from her in a morning.
